description: CN-10 — the ONLY case distinguishing the ratified Pole C route-region model from Pole A. §20.8.4 keep-alive re-entry: enter the route, dwell, leave, re-enter within TTL; the `<timer>` SHALL resume AT PHASE rather than restart at 0, and pre-leave region cell values SHALL be intact. CODES HALF ONLY. ⚠️ S314 CORRECTION — an earlier revision of this description (authored the same session) also asserted "there SHALL be no cold re-fetch", carried over from the debate artifact's CN-10 spec. That assertion is REMOVED for two independent reasons. (1) This fixture has no `<request>`, so it could never exercise it. (2) More importantly it is WRONG as stated: §20.8.4's cache is SQL-server-load-scoped throughout — keyed by "only-the-params that reach SQL", with each sub-payload's table read-set derived via `extractSelectProjection()` and invalidated by one Postgres AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger per read table. A `<request>` is an HTTP fetch (§6.7.7 / §60) with no table read-set and no trigger; it CANNOT participate in that cache. So keep-alive does not suppress `<request>` re-run, and §6.7.2.1's "a body associated with a route region SHALL run on every route-enter, including the first" applies to it unconditionally. The debate artifact's CN-10 spec (`<page keep-alive>` + `<request>` + mount counter + timer, asserting "no cold fetch") assumes the opposite and is inconsistent with §20.8.4's mechanism — do NOT restore the `<request>` to this fixture without a ruling. The judge's standing warning was: "Author it now, mark Nominal — if it is never authored, the ruling silently becomes A." It was unauthorable in ANY form until S314 because `<page keep-alive>` did not compile (E-PAGE-INVALID-ATTR), so the codes half would have asserted the OPPOSITE of the ruling. bryan's S314 ruling admitting the fifth attribute unblocked it; this pins the authoring surface now and names the builds the behavioural half waits on, so the ruling can no longer decay into Pole A unobserved.
rationale: §20.8.4: "A kept-alive route's server-load payload is cached client-side, keyed by route + params, and returning reuses the cache under a stale-while-revalidate policy." §20.8.8 (ratified Pole C, S313) makes the route region a third lifecycle owner keyed by `(route, params)`, which is precisely what makes keep-alive expressible without carving an exception into §6.7.2's memoryless-remount SHALL. The declaration compiles clean today; the cache and the at-phase timer resume do not exist yet. The cache's scope is the SQL server load ONLY — see the description's S314 correction.
runtime-half-ref: TWO builds owed, both open: (1) §20.8.4 keep-alive runtime cache + §52/§38 invalidation wiring — still Nominal, no cache exists; (2) the route-region leave/enter edges (`g-route-timer-poll-not-stopped-on-soft-nav`, HIGH) — a route `<timer>` is neither stopped on leave nor restarted on re-entry, so 'resumes at phase' has nothing to resume. Authoring the runtime half before BOTH land would add a permanently-red case (pa-base §8 cry-wolf).
